content.what_it_is: Fortran INPUT_READ module implementing generic dispatch to integer, float, logical, and string readers. Each checks file existence, searches for an exact key with READ_VALUE, classifies the extracted token, and converts it; READ_VALUE reopens and linearly scans unit 10 for every key (lines 52-350).

equations.ref: value extraction after exact key match

unresolved: READ_VALUE returns on a successful match at line 299 without closing unit 10; CLOSE(10) exists only on the EOF path at line 306. Repeated reads therefore reopen an already-connected hard-coded unit (lines 282-306).

The type checker recognizes a float only if a dot exists at lines 340-345. Valid exponent notation without a dot, such as 1E-3, passes the numeric alphabet test at lines 319,332-337 but is classified INTEGER, conflicting with READ_FLOAT (lines 155-165).
The first ! is stripped without quote handling and the first = is always the separator at lines 290-298, so string values containing those characters cannot round-trip.

READ_LOGICAL warns for values other than single-letter T/F at lines 204-211 but then accepts every value beginning with uppercase T at lines 213-214; lowercase true becomes false while unrelated T-prefixed text becomes true.
VAL_READ and VAL_TYPE are shared module variables at lines 61-62, making the public readers non-reentrant under concurrent calls.
